text: That evening: Watson says the opening was too small to matter
why: In the gathering darkness at the inn, Watson dismisses the ventilator as a small, not unusual opening that a rat could hardly pass through; this is fair paraphrase.

text: What was the ventilator really put there for? — nothing sinister: a small opening between two rooms is not unusual
id: q.why_ventilator=nothing sinister: a small opening between two rooms is not unusual
why: This is Watson's stated view in ¶205, offered as a possibility after Holmes called the ventilator singular.

text: What, if anything, came through the ventilator into that room? — slim enough for an opening so small that a rat could hardly pass through
why: Holmes has drawn attention to the ventilator as a link between the rooms, and the hedged 'if anything' asserts nothing; that anything passing through must be slim follows directly from the opening's stated size.
